fields.columns: | columns event.time, event.type, site.name, agent.uuid, src.process.storyline.id, src.process.user, src.process.uid, src.process.cmdline, src.ip.address, src.port.number, dst.ip.address, dst.port.number, src.process.parent.cmdline, tgt.process.cmdline
fields.description: Detects a potential command line flag anomaly related to "regsvr32" in which the "/i" flag is used without the "/n" which should be uncommon.
fields.name: Potential Regsvr32 Commandline Flag Anomaly
fields.notes:
- To move around freely without attracting too much attention, attackers often use reliable software (one of the favorites is psexec) that looks normal in an enterprise environment.
- Use the following aggregate to easily group by endpoint: `| group array_agg_distinct(dst.ip.address) by endpoint.name, src.process.cmdline`
fields.query: event.type="Process Creation" and (endpoint.os="windows" and ((tgt.process.image.path contains "\regsvr32.exe" and (tgt.process.cmdline contains " -i:" or tgt.process.cmdline contains " /i:" or tgt.process.cmdline contains " –i:" or tgt.process.cmdline contains " —i:" or tgt.process.cmdline contains " ―i:")) and (not tgt.process.cmdline contains " -n " or tgt.process.cmdline contains " /n " or tgt.process.cmdline contains " –n " or tgt.process.cmdline contains " —n " or tgt.process.cmdline contains " ―n ")))
